newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BULLISH PHASE SENDS BUCHAREST BOURSE HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: BULLISH PHASE SENDS BUCHAREST BOURSE HIGHER.

text.p: Bucharest bourse average
prices, volumes and turnover moved higher on Tuesday under a
strong buying interest extended from the previous day. Two
independent indices touched new highs for the year.
Seventeen companies had stronger average prices, 10 fell
and one remained flat. Ten companies had no trade and two were
suspended. Some of the stocks closed higher in late trading.
"Foreign investors haven't lost interest despite the tax on
portfolio deals which is viewed as prohibitive," said a trader.
The government announced on Monday changes in proposed
portfolio investment rules, saying it replaced a four percent
capital gains tax with a 1.5 percent portfolio transaction fee.
"Apparently, not all foreigners heard about the tax,"
another trader said. "But the moment they do we might see a
fall of the market and this could happen any day now."
Volumes grew to 4.6 million shares from 3.9 million and
turnover was 2.7 billion lei higher at 17.7 billion.
The unofficial VAB and BIG indices, based on average prices
and capitalisation, jumped 3.4 percent each from Monday. The
BIG first-tier index was 3.98 percent up at 4,539.86 points.
The first tier, including six listings, dominated trading,
accounting for around 88 percent of turnover. Five high-caps
saw higher average prices and three firmed at the close.
Fertiliser maker Azomures put on 150 lei to end
at 3,850 and Oltchim chemical plant closed 50 lei
firmer at 3,300. Pharmaceuticals company Terapia
gained 350 lei and closed at 6,500.
Arctic refrigerator maker lost 100 lei to end at
3,800, fertiliser maker Sofert shed 14,000 lei to a
49,000 lei close and Antibiotice pharmaceuticals had
a 300 lei weaker close at 5,100.
On the second tier, Policolor dye maker was in
the focus, with 1.3 billion lei in turnover. It closed 150 lei
higher at 5,850.
